public.prompt: A normalized Angular 17 store publishes entity references to several selectors. It mutates one cached user in place, so an `OnPush` card stays stale; profiling shows unchanged cards currently prune correctly. Updated consumers need one coherent snapshot while unaffected cards should keep skipping work. Which store contract fixes the boundary?

options.label: Keep mutating the cached entity, but clone it inside the dashboard selector before passing it to matching cards.
Keep the cached entity reference and increment one version input passed to every card after any entity write.
Replace the cached entity immutably and publish its new reference while preserving every unchanged entity reference.

answerProof.summary: Replacing the normalized entity at the store boundary publishes one coherent new identity to all affected consumers while unchanged references continue enabling OnPush pruning.
decisiveConstraints: Every selector must observe one coherent identity for the updated entity.
Unchanged entity references must remain stable so unrelated cards can keep pruning.
The updated entity must reach OnPush inputs with a new object identity.

claims.statement: Angular 17 does not invoke OnPush change detection for a mutated object input when its reference is preserved.

optionRationales.explanation: The dashboard can receive a new wrapper, but other selectors still observe the mutated cached identity and no single store snapshot represents the update.
optionRationales.plausibility: A selector-local clone gives the affected dashboard card a new input reference.
optionRationales.falsifyingConstraint: Several selectors must observe one coherent updated entity identity.

optionRationales.explanation: The changing version can refresh the stale card, but passing it everywhere makes every card an update candidate after unrelated entity writes.
optionRationales.plausibility: A primitive version change reliably notifies OnPush inputs after a store write.
optionRationales.falsifyingConstraint: Cards backed by unchanged entities should retain their current pruning behavior.

optionRationales.explanation: The immutable replacement becomes the shared updated snapshot, while stable identities for other entities preserve their cards' bailout path.
